dataset.name: Aggregated carbon dioxide flux and hydrometeorology data from an Amazonian palm swamp peatland in Peru: 2018, 2019, and 2022
description: This dataset contains eddy covariance carbon dioxide flux and hydrometeorological measurements made in an Amazonian palm swamp peatland near Iquitos, Peru. These data have been aggregated from half-hourly observations that are available from AmeriFlux (https://ameriflux.lbl.gov/; site PE-QFR). These data files are CSV (comma separated values) format and can be imported using Matlab, R, or Excel. Three full years of data are reported (2018, 2019 and 2022) during which time there were large differences in annual net ecosystem carbon dioxide exchange. The gap was caused by instrument malfunction and extended delays in repairs because of the Covid-19 pandemic. This research was conducted to better understand the carbon cycle of tropical peatlands, and was supported by the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Biological and Environmental Research, Terrestrial Ecosystem Science Program, under Award Number DE-SC0020167.

measurementTechnique:
This data product was produced from gap-filled half-hourly flux and hydrometeorological data.
Carbon dioxide flux and hydrometeorological data were gap-filled using the marginal distribution sampling approach using ReddyProc. Long gaps in air temperature and humidity data caused by sensor failure were filled using random forest regression.
For computing statistics, daytime and nighttime were identified when photosynthetically active radiation was greater and less than 5 μmol m−2 s−1.
